main_body: Large steampunk building: a corrugated grey-steel roof slope (rows 47-91) with skylights, a flat ridge deck with a railing, and a brick wall below with arched windows, a steel double door and copper pipes (rows 92-135).
top_band: The roof reads as a large foreshortened slope: a light ridge/eave edge at row 49 (L158), then grey corrugated roof from rows 50-90 (L122 to L95), with a darker railing band at rows 53-58. There is no single clean flat top band.
evidence: The roof is a big sloped surface seen from above, like the hip roofs on the references. It sits clearly above a separate vertical brick wall. The orange gutter at row 92 acts as the front-edge line, and the dark row 91 just above it is the shadow under the eave. The arched windows and the door are drawn inset with dark inner edges. The roof carries a ridge deck and skylights, so it is not a flat band hat over an elevation. The wall is a vertical face, but the roof and wall are both present.

style.evidence: The measured facts are weaker than the references. The candidate has 37 distinct colours against 185 and 66, and a median of 9 colours per tile against 18 and 11. Its dark edge pixels are 89% neutral, while the references are 7-9% neutral, so the outline is a neutral near-black line (#14181f, #1f2630, #1d1722) rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material. That is the sticker look. The roof ramp has about 5 grey steps but is mostly vertical stripes with a few rust dots, and the brick and windows have some detail. Flat fills are low at 1%. Overall it looks thinner than the references because of the neutral outline and the lower colour count.
